time_convention: t = frame / fps; frame = round(t * fps); t=0 is frame 0
pixel_convention: x right, y down, origin top-left of the 1080x1080 frame, full resolution

camera.motion: static (phase correlation on the boathouse: shift < 0.02 px for all frames; mean abs diff of the sky/land area < 0.3 grey levels)
camera.view: eye-level view across a small lake toward a wooden boathouse; camera just above the water, looking roughly horizontally

perspective_cues.water_plane: lake surface fills y > ~600 (near shore line y~600-650 behind the boat); water is a horizontal plane, objects further away have their waterline higher in the image
perspective_cues.horizon: not visible (hills and trees block it); far shoreline/hill foot at y~450-530, so the horizon is roughly y~450-500 at most (camera nearly level)

objects.name: rowboat
objects.description: white/light-grey wooden rowboat with dark blue interior and a vertical stem post at the bow; the only moving object
objects.partial: frames 0-54: stern beyond the right image edge (only the bow part visible; at frame 0 only x 990-1079)
objects.motion: translates right-to-left (bow leading, bow points left) along a line roughly parallel to the image plane, in front of (closer than) the jetty; apparent size constant within ~2-3%
objects.reference_point: ref_x/ref_y = centre of the full-boat image box (bow_x .. bow_x+length, top_y .. waterline_y); ref_x for frames 0-54 uses the extrapolated length 647.9 px. bow_x (stem tip) is the most precise point.
objects.reflection: mirror image in the water below y~757 is NOT part of the boat; excluded from masks
